references.text: Jesus warns that stumbling blocks (skandala) must come. In [ref:Matt 18:7|Matthew 18:7], Jesus gives the same warning with almost identical wording: "Woe to the world because of stumbling blocks! Stumbling blocks must come, but woe to the person through whom the stumbling block comes!"

Also in [ref:Mark 9:42|Mark 9:42], Jesus strongly warns against becoming a cause for others to fall, especially for little ones who believe – a close parallel passage to this warning about stumbling blocks.

In [ref:Matt 26:24|Matthew 26:24], Jesus pronounces a similar "woe" over Judas: The Son of Man goes as it is written about him, but woe to the person who betrays him. Same principle: God's plan is fulfilled, yet the one used as an instrument for evil is still responsible.

Paul discusses the same theme in [ref:Rom 14:13|Romans 14:13], where he urges believers not to place any stumbling block or obstacle in the way of their brother – a practical application of Jesus' warning about stumbling blocks.

In [ref:Rom 16:17|Romans 16:17], Paul warns against those who cause divisions and stumbling blocks (skandala) contrary to the teaching they have received – the same Greek word is used as in Jesus' warning here.

In [ref:1 Kor 11:19|1 Corinthians 11:19], Paul says that there "must" be divisions among you, so that it may become clear which of you are genuine. This reflects the same divine "must" (dei/anankes) that Jesus speaks of when he says that stumbling blocks must come.

In [ref:Matt 13:41|Matthew 13:41], Jesus speaks of how at the end of the age, the Son of Man will send his angels, and they will gather out of his kingdom all things that cause stumbling (skandala) – the final removal of those stumbling blocks which Jesus here says must come.
In [ref:2 Pet 2:1-2|2 Peter 2:1-2], Peter warns against false teachers who will come among believers and lead many astray – a fulfillment of Jesus' words that stumbling blocks will inevitably come.
